sheets.title: OWASP Top 10 (2021)
sheets.desc: The ten most critical web application security risk categories, 2021 edition.

items.what: Users act outside their permissions, e.g. IDOR: changing an ID in the URL to view someone else's data.
Sensitive data exposed through weak or missing encryption, e.g. plaintext passwords, old TLS.
Untrusted input interpreted as code: SQL injection, command injection, XSS. Use parameterised queries and output encoding.
Flaws in the design itself; fix with threat modelling and secure design patterns.
Default credentials, verbose errors, open cloud storage, unnecessary features enabled.
Using libraries/frameworks with known vulnerabilities. Track and patch dependencies.
Weak passwords allowed, no MFA, broken session handling, credential stuffing.

items.cmd: A08 Software and Data Integrity Failures
items.what: Untrusted updates, insecure CI/CD, insecure deserialisation.

items.cmd: A09 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
items.what: Attacks go unnoticed because events aren't logged or alerted on.
The server is tricked into fetching attacker-chosen URLs, e.g. internal cloud metadata.

sheets.title: Incident response steps
sheets.desc: Based on the NIST SP 800-61 lifecycle. Document everything with timestamps.

items.what: IR plan, contacts, roles, logging enabled, backups tested, tools ready before anything happens.
Validate the alert, determine scope and severity, collect evidence (logs, memory, disk) and preserve chain of custody.
Stop the spread: isolate hosts, disable compromised accounts, block malicious IPs/domains. Short-term then long-term.
Remove the root cause: malware, persistence, backdoors; patch the exploited vulnerability; reset credentials.
Restore from clean backups, bring systems back carefully, monitor closely for reinfection.
Lessons-learned meeting, update playbooks and detections, report to stakeholders/regulators as required (in India, CERT-In reporting rules may apply).

sheets.title: Password & 2FA hygiene
sheets.desc: Simple habits that block most account takeovers.

items.what: Bitwarden, KeePassXC, 1Password etc. One strong master password, unique passwords everywhere else.
Length beats complexity: 4 to 5 random words is stronger and easier to remember than P@ssw0rd!
One leaked site shouldn't unlock your email, bank and Instagram.
Prefer an authenticator app or passkey/security key over SMS OTP.
Store 2FA recovery codes offline or in your password manager.
No bank, courier, or government official will ever need your OTP or PIN.
Use haveibeenpwned.com and change any exposed passwords.
Your email resets every other account, so give it the strongest protection.
Auto-updates on, screen lock on, apps only from official stores.
